thermo.ideal_gas_law.title: Ideal gas law (P v = R T)
assumptions: Ideal gas. Density rho = 1/v.
method_references: Ideal gas law P v = R T

thermo.compressibility_factor.title: Compressibility factor (Z = P v / (R T))
assumptions: Z = 1 for an ideal gas; departures measure real-gas behaviour.

thermo.specific_heats.title: Specific heats from R and gamma
assumptions: Ideal gas, constant specific heats: cp - cv = R and gamma = cp/cv.

thermo.ideal_gas_energy.title: Ideal-gas internal energy and enthalpy changes
assumptions: Ideal gas, constant specific heats. Enter delta_T in K or delta_degC.
method_references: du = cv dT; dh = cp dT (ideal gas)

thermo.ideal_gas_entropy.title: Ideal-gas entropy change (constant specific heats)
assumptions: Ideal gas, constant specific heats (second T-ds / Maxwell relation, integrated).
method_references: ds = cp dT/T - R dP/P (ideal gas)

thermo.fluid_state_TP.title: Real-fluid state at given T and P

variables.name: fluid
variables.desc: CoolProp fluid name, e.g. Water, R134a, Air

variables.name: h
variables.desc: specific enthalpy (signed: negative at low T)

variables.name: u
variables.desc: specific internal energy (signed: negative at low T)

assumptions: Full CoolProp state from T and P (u = h - P/rho). For a liquid the density varies only weakly with T; a gas example is used so every input is invertible.
method_references: CoolProp reference equation of state (via common.fluid_state)

thermo.fluid_state_TQ.title: Real-fluid two-phase state at given T and quality

variables.name: fluid
variables.desc: CoolProp fluid name, e.g. Water, R134a, Air

variables.name: T
variables.desc: saturation temperature (inside the fluid saturation range)

assumptions: Two-phase state from saturation temperature T and quality Q via common.fluid_state (CoolProp). h = h_f + Q h_fg.
method_references: Lever rule h = h_f + Q (h_g - h_f) via common.fluid_state

thermo.mixture_quality.title: Two-phase quality from a specific-volume lever rule
assumptions: v_f and v_g are the saturated liquid and vapour values at the mixture pressure or temperature (from tables or fluid_state_TQ). The same lever rule applies to h, s and u.

thermo.boundary_work_isobaric.title: Boundary work of a constant-pressure process

thermo.boundary_work_isothermal.title: Boundary work of an isothermal ideal-gas process
assumptions: Ideal gas, constant temperature (W = P1 V1 ln(V2/V1) = m R T ln(V2/V1)). Inverting for V1 has two roots (the other is on the compression side); the root nearest the example is returned.

thermo.boundary_work_polytropic.title: Boundary work of a polytropic process (P V^n = const)
assumptions: P V^n = constant. n = 1 is the isothermal case (use boundary_work_isothermal); n = 0 isobaric; n = gamma isentropic (ideal gas).

thermo.first_law_closed.title: First law for a closed system (Q - W = dU)
assumptions: Q in and W out are positive.

thermo.cv_energy_balance.title: Steady-flow energy balance per unit mass (control volume)

variables.name: w
variables.desc: shaft work per unit mass (positive = out)

assumptions: Steady flow, one inlet and one outlet, per unit mass. Neglect a term by setting its pair equal (V1 = V2 or z1 = z2).

thermo.nozzle_diffuser.title: Nozzle/diffuser exit velocity (adiabatic, no work)
assumptions: Adiabatic, no shaft work, no elevation change: V2 = sqrt(V1^2 + 2(h1 - h2)). A nozzle lowers h to raise V; a diffuser raises h to lower V.

thermo.turbine_work.title: Turbine work output (first law)

variables.name: w_out
variables.desc: turbine work output per unit mass

assumptions: Adiabatic turbine, kinetic and potential changes neglected.

thermo.compressor_work.title: Compressor/pump work input (first law)
assumptions: Adiabatic compressor/pump, kinetic and potential changes neglected.

thermo.throttle.title: Throttling (adiabatic) valve: enthalpy is constant
assumptions: Adiabatic throttle, no work, kinetic and potential changes neglected: h2 = h1.

thermo.mixing_chamber.title: Adiabatic mixing chamber outlet enthalpy
assumptions: Adiabatic mixing, no work, kinetic and potential changes neglected; mass balance m3 = mdot1 + mdot2.
method_references: mdot1 h1 + mdot2 h2 = (mdot1 + mdot2) h_mix

thermo.transient_filling.title: Adiabatic charging of an evacuated rigid tank from a line
assumptions: Initially evacuated rigid tank filled adiabatically from an ideal-gas line at constant T_line, cp/cv constant: the inflowing enthalpy shows up as internal energy, so u2 = h_line and T2 = gamma T_line.
method_references: Adiabatic charging of an evacuated tank: T2 = gamma T_line (landmark)

thermo.transient_discharge.title: Reversible adiabatic blowdown of a rigid tank

variables.name: T2
variables.desc: final temperature of the gas remaining in the tank

assumptions: Slow (reversible, adiabatic) discharge: the gas remaining in the rigid tank expands isentropically, T2 = T1 (P2/P1)^((gamma-1)/gamma).
method_references: Isentropic expansion of the gas remaining in the tank

thermo.carnot_efficiency.title: Carnot efficiency
assumptions: Reversible cycle between T_H and T_L.

thermo.cop.title: Coefficient of performance (refrigerator and heat pump)

variables.name: Q_L
variables.desc: heat removed from the cold space

variables.name: Q_H
variables.desc: heat delivered to the hot space

assumptions: COP_ref = Q_L/W_in; COP_hp = Q_H/W_in. The first law gives Q_H = Q_L + W_in for any cycle (not only a reversible one), so COP_hp = COP_ref + 1 holds generally.

thermo.cop_carnot.title: Carnot COPs of a refrigerator and heat pump
assumptions: Reversible cycle.
method_references: Carnot COPs: T_L/(T_H - T_L) and T_H/(T_H - T_L)

thermo.entropy_generation.title: Entropy generation (per unit mass)

variables.name: q
variables.desc: heat transfer into the system per unit mass

variables.name: T_b
variables.desc: boundary temperature at which q is transferred

assumptions: Closed system: s_gen = (s2 - s1) - q/T_b >= 0 for a real process (negative means the process is impossible).

thermo.isentropic_efficiency_turbine.title: Turbine isentropic efficiency
assumptions: Expansion (h1 > h2a > h2s): eta_t = actual work / isentropic work.
method_references: Turbine isentropic efficiency eta_t = (h1 - h2a)/(h1 - h2s)

thermo.isentropic_efficiency_compressor.title: Compressor isentropic efficiency
assumptions: Compression (h1 < h2s < h2a): eta_c = isentropic work / actual work.
method_references: Compressor isentropic efficiency eta_c = (h2s - h1)/(h2a - h1)

thermo.exergy.title: Specific flow exergy (with kinetic and potential terms)

variables.name: z
variables.desc: elevation above the dead state (0 if negligible)

assumptions: Specific flow exergy psi = (h - h0) - T0 (s - s0) + V^2/2 + g z, with the potential term using standard gravity g = 9.80665 m/s^2 (common.g0()). Set V = 0 and z = 0 to drop the kinetic/potential terms.

thermo.second_law_efficiency.title: Second-law efficiency
assumptions: eta_II = 1 - (exergy destroyed)/(exergy supplied).

thermo.gas_mixture.title: Gas-mixture mole/mass fractions and molar mass
assumptions: Binary mixture. mf1 = (y1 M1)/(y1 M1 + y2 M2); M_mix = y1 M1 + y2 M2. The mixture gas constant is R_mix = 8314.5/M_mix [J/(kg K)].
method_references: Mole/mass fraction conversion and mixture molar mass

thermo.clapeyron.title: Clapeyron equation (saturation pressure slope)
assumptions: This is the Maxwell relation (dP/dT)_v = (ds/dv)_T evaluated along the saturation curve, equal to h_fg/(T v_fg). The four Maxwell relations are (dT/dv)_s = -(dP/ds)_v, (dT/dP)_s = (dv/ds)_P, (dP/dT)_v = (ds/dv)_T, (dv/dT)_P = -(ds/dP)_T.
method_references: Clapeyron equation / Maxwell relation along saturation

thermo.clausius_clapeyron.title: Clausius-Clapeyron equation (ideal-gas vapour)
assumptions: Ideal-gas vapour with v_g >> v_f and constant h_fg.

thermo.joule_thomson.title: Joule-Thomson coefficient (finite difference on enthalpy)

variables.name: fluid
variables.desc: CoolProp fluid name, e.g. Water, R134a, Air

variables.name: cp
variables.desc: cp from the enthalpy finite difference

procedure.python:
def _joule_thomson(values):
    """Joule-Thomson coefficient mu = (dT/dP)_h by central finite difference on h (CoolProp states).

    mu = -(dh/dP)_T / (dh/dT)_P, with (dh/dP)_T and (dh/dT)_P evaluated by central differences on
    common.fluid_state; the denominator is approximately cp. Stated as a numerical finite difference.
    The four stencil states must share one single phase, otherwise a phase boundary is being straddled
    and the finite difference is meaningless (raises MechError).
    """
    fluid = _fluid_name(values['fluid'])
    T, P = values['T'], values['P']
    dT, dP = 0.5, 1000.0
    s_pp = common.fluid_state(fluid, T=T, P=P + dP)
    s_pm = common.fluid_state(fluid, T=T, P=P - dP)
    s_tp = common.fluid_state(fluid, T=T + dT, P=P)
    s_tm = common.fluid_state(fluid, T=T - dT, P=P)
    phases = {s_pp['phase'], s_pm['phase'], s_tp['phase'], s_tm['phase']}
    if len(phases) != 1 or next(iter(phases)) in ('twophase', 'unknown', None):
        raise MechError('Joule-Thomson coefficient needs a single-phase state; the +/-dT/dP stencil at '
                        f'(T = {T:g} K, P = {P:g} Pa) crosses a phase boundary '
                        f'({sorted(map(str, phases))}). Move the state away from the saturation curve.')
    dh_dP = (s_pp['h'] - s_pm['h']) / (2.0 * dP)
    dh_dT = (s_tp['h'] - s_tm['h']) / (2.0 * dT)
    return {'mu': -dh_dP / dh_dT, 'cp': dh_dT}

assumptions: mu = (dT/dP)_h = -(dh/dP)_T/(dh/dT)_P, evaluated by central finite difference on common.fluid_state (CoolProp) with dT = 0.5 K and dP = 1000 Pa, so it is a numerical derivative, stated as such. mu > 0 cools on throttling; mu < 0 heats.
method_references: Joule-Thomson coefficient by finite difference on h (CoolProp states)

thermo.fluid_saturation_dome.title: Saturation curve (T-s / P-h dome) from common.saturation

variables.name: fluid
variables.desc: CoolProp fluid name, e.g. Water, R134a, Air

variables.name: dome
variables.desc: arrays T, P, s_f, s_g, h_f, h_g (all SI) along the saturation curve

procedure.python:
def _saturation_dome(values):
    """Saturation curve points from common.saturation, for a T-s / P-h chart."""
    fluid = _fluid_name(values['fluid'])
    rng = values['T_range']
    if not isinstance(rng, list) or len(rng) != 2:
        raise MechError('T_range: give [T_min (K), T_max (K)]')
    T_min, T_max = float(rng[0]), float(rng[1])
    if T_min >= T_max:
        raise MechError('T_range needs T_min < T_max, inside the fluid saturation range')
    N = 40
    Ts = [T_min + (T_max - T_min) * i / (N - 1) for i in range(N)]
    Ps, sfs, sgs, hfs, hgs = [], [], [], [], []
    for T in Ts:
        sat = common.saturation(fluid, T=T)
        Ps.append(sat['P'])
        sfs.append(sat['liquid']['s'])
        sgs.append(sat['vapour']['s'])
        hfs.append(sat['liquid']['h'])
        hgs.append(sat['vapour']['h'])
    return {'P_min': Ps[0], 'P_max': Ps[-1],
            'dome': {'T': Ts, 'P': Ps, 's_f': sfs, 's_g': sgs, 'h_f': hfs, 'h_g': hgs}}

assumptions: Saturated liquid and vapour states from common.saturation (CoolProp) at 40 evenly spaced temperatures in [T_min, T_max]; T_max must be below the critical temperature.
